price_basis: Per ADS (1 ADS = 8 ordinary shares). Verified live from Yahoo Finance 2026-07-26.
data_revision_note: REVISED 2026-07-26: Corrected a material net-debt error in the prior same-day model. The prior model computed net debt as total_debt (259,996) minus cash (131,530) only = net debt of 128,466 RMB M, ignoring Alibaba's short-term investments and other treasury investments -- where most of the balance-sheet war chest actually sits. Per the FY2026 20-F MD&A (Liquidity and Capital Resources, 'As of March 31, 2026, we had cash and cash equivalents of RMB131,530 million..., short-term investments and other treasury investments that are unrestricted for withdrawal and use of RMB155,236 million... and RMB234,058 million... respectively, totaling RMB520,824 million'), the correct treasury position nets to a NET CASH position of RMB 260,828M (520,824 total liquid/near-liquid assets minus 259,996 total debt), not a net debt burden. This is a swing of RMB 389,294M in the equity bridge. All operating assumptions (FCF bases, growth paths, WACCs, terminal growth rates, normalized EBITDA basis, probability weights, current price, FX, share counts, hurdle rate) are UNCHANGED. The historical EV/EBITDA series (used to calibrate exit-multiple caps) and the exit-multiple caps themselves were also recomputed on the same net-of-investment-portfolio basis for consistency, since they were previously overstated the same way by omitting short-term/treasury investments from the EV bridge. Net effect: exit-multiple caps come down materially (the corrected 'normal-year' EV/EBITDA range is lower once more cash is stripped out of EV), while the net-cash addition to the equity bridge pushes value up -- the two effects partially offset. See valuation.base/bull/bear and entry_price sections below for the reconciled result.

inputs.net_debt_sign_convention: Positive = net debt (cash outflow item, subtracted from EV). Negative = net CASH (added to EV to reach equity value). net_debt_rmb_mn = total_debt (259,996) - [cash (131,530) + unrestricted short-term investments (155,236) + unrestricted other treasury investments (234,058)] = 259,996 - 520,824 = -260,828, i.e. a net CASH position of RMB 260,828M. Balance-sheet gross alternative (ST investments 155,310 + other treasury investments at fair value 238,075 = 524,915 total, giving net cash of 264,919) was considered but the MD&A 'unrestricted for withdrawal and use' basis of 520,824 is used throughout as the more decision-useful, liquidity-tested figure.
inputs.fx_note: Live USD/CNY rate as of 2026-07-26, per user instruction. RMB has strengthened materially vs the 7.25 rate used in the 2026-06-30 model; this alone raises USD-converted intrinsic values by ~7% relative to an unchanged RMB valuation.

historical_growth.fcf_cagr_note: FY2026 FCF was -RMB 46,609M (negative trough driven by RMB 126B AI capex and quick-commerce subsidies). Standard CAGR cannot be computed from a negative terminal value. FCF history FY2020-FY2026: [130,914; 172,662; 98,874; 171,663; 156,210; 73,870; -46,609] RMB M. FY2020-FY2025 average = RMB 134,032M. Normalized base = RMB 120,000M (10% haircut to reflect near-term capex overhang).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (2.5%) is far below Revenue 5yr CAGR (7.4%) and EPS 3yr CAGR (16.8%). Divergence is explained by: (1) massive share buybacks reducing equity per share denominator effects and reinvestment mix, (2) FY2026 investment cycle compressing retained earnings, (3) a corrected FY2017 equity base (278,799 RMB M, down from a previously overstated 566,578) that raises the LONGER-horizon (9yr, FY2017-FY2026) equity CAGR to 16.0% -- but this window is dominated by the initial low base and is not representative of steady-state compounding. Per the trough-FCF framework, equity CAGR is not used as the primary growth anchor -- FCF recovery trajectory is modeled explicitly by scenario. FCF CAGR is flagged N/A due to negative terminal year.
historical_growth.metrics_correction_note: BABA_Metrics.csv was rebuilt 2026-07-26 from audited FY2026 20-F data. Key corrections vs the prior model: FY2017 equity corrected to 278,799 RMB M (was 566,578); FY2026 cash corrected to 131,530 and total debt to 259,996 RMB M; diluted weighted-avg shares FY2026 = 19,235M ordinary (~2,404.4M ADS), down slightly from the prior model's 19,319M ordinary / 2,414.9M ADS due to continued buybacks. A separate same-day correction (2026-07-26, see data_revision_note) fixed net debt to net the full unrestricted short-term + other treasury investment portfolio (net CASH of 260,828), not cash alone (which understated net cash by 389,294 RMB M). None of these corrections materially change the 3yr/5yr equity CAGRs used for divergence checking, since neither window touches FY2017.

valuation_philosophy.approach: Trough-FCF Mid-Cycle Normalization with Exit-Multiple Cap
valuation_philosophy.summary: FY2026 is an intentional investment trough -- not structural demand decline. Alibaba deployed RMB 126B in AI/cloud capex (part of a stated RMB 380B+ three-year programme, guided to potentially 'overshoot') and poured subsidies into Taobao Instant Commerce to compete with Meituan, collapsing FCF to a RMB 46,609M outflow. These are discretionary investment choices, and July 2026 developments (quick-commerce loss-per-order roughly halved from peak, guided ~50% cut in FY2027 quick-commerce investment, SAMR's June 2026 anti-subsidy rules, AIDC EBITA loss narrowing 96% YoY, Cloud Intelligence Group Q4 external revenue +40% turbocharged by the Apple Intelligence/Qwen partnership) all support a faster-than-previously-modeled recovery path. Anchoring the DCF base year on FY2026 reported FCF would systematically under-value the business (the inverse of the classic peak-FCF trap). The model retains a NORMALIZED (mid-cycle) FCF base of RMB 120,000M for the base case: a ~10.5% discount to the FY2020-FY2025 average of RMB 134,032M, still reflecting continued elevated capex through FY2028 despite the encouraging de-escalation signals. Bull case raised slightly to RMB 138,000M (toward FY2024 actual FCF of 156,210M, reflecting the July 2026 Apple/Qwen catalyst and faster subsidy war resolution). Bear case raised modestly to RMB 68,000M (near-FY2025-trough but slightly below it, reflecting that geopolitical/legal tail risks -- DoD 1260H, Anthropic securities investigation -- could still reopen a deeper investment or legal-cost cycle even if the base/bull scenarios' catalysts are already visible). An exit-multiple cap (min of Gordon Growth TV vs EV/EBITDA cap on normalized EBITDA) prevents any scenario from implying multiples the market has never sustainably paid for BABA. This cap remains binding in the base and bull cases; Gordon Growth is more conservative and binds in the bear case. REVISED 2026-07-26: exit-multiple caps were re-derived (down from 9.0/11.5/6.0 to 7.0/9.5/4.5) after correcting the historical EV/EBITDA series to net the full investment portfolio out of EV, not just cash -- see exit_multiple_cap.rationale below. All FCF bases, growth rates, and WACCs are unchanged.

wacc_rationale.note: WACC held unchanged from the prior model despite the July 2026 news flow being net positive (DoD interim relief, DOJ non-prosecution settlement, H200 licensing, Apple/Qwen deal). These developments are real risk-reduction, but each remains only PARTIALLY resolved as of 2026-07-26: the DoD 1260H litigation is ongoing (interim relief only, not a final ruling), the Rosen Law Firm securities investigation into the Anthropic distillation allegations is newly active (a fresh, uncosted overhang that roughly offsets the DoD/DOJ improvement), and H200 access remains capped at 75,000 units/customer with a 25% revenue-share tax. Net effect: risk premium components are judged unchanged at this time. Base 11.5% = 4.5% risk-free + 5.0% ERP + 1.5% China/VIE/regulatory + 0.5% Pentagon CMC + 0.5% Anthropic/securities litigation overhang. Bull case (10.5%) assumes geopolitical/legal risks resolve favorably (DoD case won on Xiaomi/AMEC precedent, no securities suit filed). Bear case (13.0%) assumes China-US tensions re-escalate, the Pentagon designation is upheld, and/or a securities class action is filed and gains traction. Not revised in the 2026-07-26 net-debt correction (balance-sheet-only fix).

exit_multiple_cap.ebitda_basis_note: Average of FY2023 (175,710), FY2024 (191,668), and FY2025 (202,325) Adjusted EBITDA -- representing Alibaba's EBITDA in non-trough years. Projected to Y5 at 60% of FCF growth rates per year, then multiplied by exit multiple. Terminal value = min(Gordon Growth TV, exit multiple TV). EBITDA basis itself is unchanged by the net-debt correction.
exit_multiple_cap.rationale: REVISED 2026-07-26: the prior historical EV/EBITDA series computed EV as market cap + total debt - cash only, omitting short-term investments and other treasury investments from the EV bridge -- the same error as the net-debt bridge, and it overstated every year's multiple by the same amount. Recomputed 10yr historical EV/EBITDA using FY-end ADS closes, corrected balance-sheet data, and EV = market cap + total debt - cash - short-term investments - other treasury investments (unrestricted/reported basis; FY2017-FY2018 lack short-term investment disclosure in our extracts, so those two years remain cash-only and are flagged as such -- they fall outside the FY2022-FY2025 calibration window regardless): FY2017 25.0x (cash-only, ST-investment data unavailable), FY2018 27.7x (cash-only, ST-investment data unavailable), FY2019 25.8x, FY2020 21.8x, FY2021 19.1x (bubble peak), FY2022 9.9x, FY2023 8.3x, FY2024 4.6x, FY2025 9.6x, FY2026 16.0x (trough-EBITDA distortion, using the MD&A unrestricted total of RMB 520,824M against FY2026's depressed EBITDA). The 'normal-year' (FY2022-FY2025) EV/EBITDA range is now 4.62x-9.94x with an average of ~8.12x -- materially lower than the prior (cash-only) estimate of 6.5x-11.9x / ~10.1x, because a much larger cash-like buffer is now correctly removed from EV in every year. Base recalibrated to 7.0x (~89% of the 8.12x normal-year average, preserving the same conservative-mid-range bias as the prior model's 9.0x/10.09x ratio). Bull recalibrated to 9.5x (~97% of the 9.94x normal-year high, mirroring the prior model's bull-near-but-not-above-max logic). Bear recalibrated to 4.5x (~97% of the 4.62x normal-year low, mirroring the prior model's bear-near-floor logic). Exit cap remains binding in base and bull cases; Gordon Growth is more conservative and binds in the bear case (unchanged from the prior model's binding pattern). Current spot EV/EBITDA on normalized (avg FY23-25) EBITDA, using the corrected net-cash EV, is ~8.2x -- within the corrected normal-year range, confirming the caps do not require multiple expansion beyond where the market already prices normalized BABA net of its full investment portfolio.

base.fcf_base_description: Normalized mid-cycle FCF; 10.5% discount to FY2020-FY2025 average of 134,032M to reflect continued AI capex through FY2028
base.growth_narrative: Y1 (+22%): FCF begins recovering as quick-commerce subsidies moderate (loss-per-order already halved from peak, guided ~50% FY2027 investment cut) and Cloud Intelligence Group AI revenue scales (external cloud revenue +40% in Q4 FY2026). Y2 (+18%): AIDC reaches break-even (EBITA loss already down 96% YoY in Q4 FY2026), removing a headwind. Y3-Y4 (+14%/+10%): capex intensity plateaus, incremental AI/Apple-driven cloud revenue flows to FCF at improving margin. Y5 (+7%): deceleration toward terminal growth as e-commerce matures. Unchanged from the 2026-07-26 pre-revision model -- this is a balance-sheet-only correction.

bull.fcf_base_description: Higher normalized base just below FY2024 actual FCF level (156,210M), reflecting faster cloud/AI monetization inflection catalyzed by the Apple/Qwen partnership
bull.growth_narrative: Faster cloud/AI commercialization following the July 2026 Apple Intelligence/Qwen deal: AI products reach 50%+ of external cloud revenue ahead of the ~1-year management target, and the Apple relationship expands. Quick commerce unit economics improve rapidly (positive by early FY2027, ahead of the end-FY2027 target) as SAMR rules take hold faster than expected. AIDC profitable in FY2027 per guidance. Anthropic securities investigation closes without a filed suit; DoD 1260H case resolved in Alibaba's favor (Xiaomi/AMEC precedent). H200 chip access expands beyond the initial 75,000-unit cap. FCF recovers sharply. Unchanged from the pre-revision model.

bear.fcf_base_description: Sustained suppression slightly below FY2025 actual level (73,870M): subsidy war re-escalates or legal/geopolitical risk deepens the investment/cost cycle
bear.growth_narrative: Subsidy war with Meituan re-escalates despite SAMR rules, or a renewed flare-up occurs given 'war without a clear winner' as of mid-2026. Rosen Law Firm securities investigation matures into a filed class action, and/or the DoD upholds the 1260H designation on appeal, triggering forced institutional selling and elevated legal costs. AI capex ROI disappoints despite the Apple deal (one contract among a much larger, diversified spend program); H200 access remains capped and insufficient for frontier-scale training. FCF recovers slowly from trough. E-commerce market share continues eroding to Douyin and PDD. Unchanged from the pre-revision model.

valuation.note: REVISED 2026-07-26: All FCF and EV/equity figures in RMB millions. Intrinsic value converted to USD per ADS: (equity_value_rmb_mn / ordinary_shares_mn) * 8 / fx_rmb_per_usd (fx = 6.7617). Net debt = total_debt (259,996) - [cash (131,530) + unrestricted short-term investments (155,236) + unrestricted other treasury investments (234,058)] = -260,828, i.e. a NET CASH position of RMB 260,828M, ADDED to enterprise value to reach equity value (not subtracted, since the prior model's net-debt figure of 128,466 omitted the investment portfolio). PV-of-FCF streams and Gordon Growth terminal values are unchanged from the pre-revision model; only the exit-multiple-cap terminal values (recalibrated caps: 7.0x/9.5x/4.5x, down from 9.0x/11.5x/6.0x) and the equity bridge (net cash added instead of net debt subtracted) have changed.

base.terminal_value_source: exit_multiple (7.0x normalized EBITDA Y5 = RMB 285,178M; binding because Gordon TV of 2,808,810 > exit TV at 11.5% WACC)

bull.terminal_value_source: exit_multiple (9.5x normalized EBITDA Y5 = RMB 321,357M; binding because Gordon TV of 4,753,533 > exit TV at 10.5% WACC)

bear.terminal_value_source: gordon_growth (bear WACC 13% makes Gordon TV 807,251 < exit multiple TV 945,264; Gordon is more conservative in bear, same binding pattern as pre-revision)

entry_price.note: REVISED 2026-07-26: Entry price = ( sum(FCF_t / 1.15^t, t=1..5) + Gordon_TV_5 / 1.15^5 + net_cash ) / ordinary_shares * 8 / fx. Gordon TV (not the exit-multiple-capped TV) is used as the fair year-5 exit value the buyer sells into, consistent with the entry-price methodology (WACC-based Gordon TV represents the price a subsequent buyer pays; only the discounting back to today uses the 15% hurdle). Net cash (260,828 RMB M) is ADDED to the bridge (prior model incorrectly subtracted a net-debt figure of 128,466). All values in USD per ADS.

base.interpretation: Base case entry ($140.48) is 25.3% ABOVE the current ADS price of $112.14 (negative 'discount' denotes entry above current). The net-cash correction raises the entry price materially versus the pre-revision figure of $116.53, because the large unrestricted investment portfolio (RMB 520,824M in liquid/near-liquid assets) is real value a buyer receives today, on top of the interim FCF and Gordon terminal value. This means a 15%-IRR buyer can pay meaningfully more than today's price and still clear the hurdle -- consistent with base intrinsic value ($129.55) also sitting above the current price. The stock is inexpensive enough in the base case that today's price already implies a forward IRR to base-case fair value comfortably above 15%.

bull.interpretation: Bull case entry ($211.44) is 88.6% above current price. If the bull scenario materializes (Apple/Qwen driven cloud re-rating, faster quick-commerce breakeven, favorable legal resolutions), the current ADS price of $112.14 provides an even larger margin of safety relative to the 15%-CAGR entry point than the pre-revision estimate, now that the full investment portfolio is correctly credited to the equity bridge.

bear.interpretation: Bear case implies severe downside (-46.7% intrinsic value loss from current price). A $56.67 entry price would be required for a 15% CAGR in the bear scenario -- 49.5% below current market price. Even after crediting the full net-cash position, this scenario still requires multiple catastrophic risks (subsidy war re-escalation, adverse DoD ruling, filed securities class action, AI capex disappointment) to materialize simultaneously for the downside to be this severe -- the large cash buffer provides a meaningful floor under the bear case relative to the pre-revision model ($32.72).

sensitivity.basis: REVISED 2026-07-26: Base case FCF = RMB 120,000M, growth rates Y1-Y5 = [22%, 18%, 14%, 10%, 7%], exit multiple cap recalibrated to 7.0x normalized EBITDA (down from 9.0x), net cash of RMB 260,828M added to the equity bridge. Values in USD per ADS.
sensitivity.matrix_note: With the recalibrated 7.0x exit multiple cap (TV = RMB 1,996,247M, fixed across the matrix), the exit cap is now binding at EVERY WACC/terminal-growth combination in the tested range -- Gordon Growth TV exceeds the exit-multiple TV even at the lowest WACC (9.5%) and lowest terminal growth (2.0%) tested. This is a direct consequence of lowering the cap from 9.0x to 7.0x following the corrected (lower) historical EV/EBITDA range. As a result, each row is now fully flat across terminal growth (no sensitivity to terminal growth at all, versus partial flatness in the pre-revision matrix), and value varies only with WACC (via the discount factor applied to the fixed exit-multiple TV and the PV of interim FCF). This is an honest byproduct of the corrected, more conservative cap -- terminal growth assumptions are effectively irrelevant to the base-case valuation once the exit-multiple discipline binds this tightly.

probability_weighted.weight_rationale: Weights held unchanged from the prior (pre-revision) model. 25% bear: meaningful but non-dominant probability that legal/geopolitical overhangs (unresolved DoD 1260H litigation, newly active Anthropic securities investigation, subsidy war re-escalation risk) deepen rather than resolve. 50% base: most likely path -- gradual FCF normalization over FY2027-FY2029 as cloud scales (Apple/Qwen deal reinforcing this), quick-commerce losses moderate per management guidance, and legal risks neither fully resolve nor escalate. 25% bull: AI monetization inflects faster than guided (Apple deal expands, cloud run-rate exceeds targets), and the DoD/securities overhangs resolve favorably as they partially have through July 2026. The net-debt correction raises the weighted IV from $118.58 to $126.35 (+6.5%) despite the lower exit-multiple caps, because the RMB 260,828M net-cash addition to the equity bridge outweighs the reduction in exit-multiple-implied terminal value in every scenario where the exit cap binds.

implied_multiples.note: REVISED 2026-07-26: EV now correctly nets the full unrestricted investment portfolio, not cash alone, so implied EV/EBITDA multiples at the (higher, net-cash-corrected) base IV are somewhat higher than the pre-revision figures even though the underlying operating value (EV) is lower -- this is because a smaller EV is being divided by the same EBITDA while a larger net-cash add-back drives up equity value and IV per share; the EV/EBITDA ratio itself moved from 11.46x to 9.72x (LOWER) on the corrected, more conservative EV base. EV/EBITDA on trough FY2026 EBITDA (RMB 113,483M) = 16.26x (down from 19.18x pre-revision) -- flagged as a trough-year outlier, not a representative sanity bound (denominator is depressed by the intentional FY2026 investment cycle, not a genuinely rich valuation). Correct comparison uses normalized EBITDA (avg FY2023-FY2025 = RMB 189,901M): 9.72x, DOWN from 11.46x pre-revision and now comfortably within (not at the top of) the corrected normal-year range of 4.62x-9.94x. P/E and P/B/P/S are essentially unchanged in ratio terms from the pre-revision figures (they were never distorted by the net-debt error, since they don't involve EV) but shift slightly because the base IV itself moved from $125.97 to $129.55.

historical_averages.series_methodology: REVISED 2026-07-26: Computed from FY-end ADS closing prices (FY2017 107.83 through FY2026 125.46, current 112.14), CSV per-year EPS_ADS_Diluted_USD, ShareholdersEquity_RMB_Mn, AdjustedEBITDA_RMB_Mn, TotalDebt/CashAndEquivalents, and (new) ShortTermInvestments_RMB_Mn/OtherTreasuryInvestments_RMB_Mn, using each fiscal year-end approximate FX rate (FY2017 6.89 through FY2026 6.90, implied from market-cap-to-PB-multiple back-solve, consistent with the pre-revision series). Market cap (RMB) = PB_multiple * ShareholdersEquity_RMB_Mn (equivalent to (price_ADS/8)*FX*ordinary_shares, cross-checked). EV = market cap + total debt - cash - short-term investments - other treasury investments (previously: market cap + total debt - cash only). FY2017-FY2018 lack short-term/other-treasury-investment data in our extracts; those two years are computed on a cash-only net-debt basis (identical to the prior series) and flagged -- they sit outside the FY2022-FY2025 calibration window used for exit-multiple caps regardless, so this data gap does not affect the caps. FY2026 uses the MD&A 'unrestricted for withdrawal and use' figures (155,236 / 234,058) for full consistency with the DCF inputs.ShortTermInvestments/OtherTreasuryInvestments for FY2026 in the CSV are the gross balance-sheet figures (155,310/238,075); the small resulting difference (net cash 260,828 MD&A basis vs 264,919 balance-sheet basis) is immaterial to the multiple (16.02x MD&A basis vs 16.0x balance-sheet basis, rounds the same).

recent_normal_years_fy2022_fy2025.note: Post-antitrust-overhaul, pre-FY2026-trough years (FY2022-FY2025) are the most relevant comparison set for a mid-cycle Alibaba, excluding both the FY2021 bubble peak and the FY2026 capex/subsidy trough. REVISED 2026-07-26: EV/EBITDA range and average recomputed netting the full investment portfolio -- materially lower than the pre-revision (cash-only) figures.

sanity_check.diagnosis: REVISED 2026-07-26: No hard sanity trip on normalized multiples, and the corrected picture is, if anything, MORE conservative than the pre-revision model on the EV/EBITDA dimension even though intrinsic value per ADS is higher. P/B 1.99x at base IV is within the recent-normal-years (FY2022-FY2025) range of 1.35x-2.30x and near the period average of ~1.88x (essentially unchanged from pre-revision, since P/B does not involve EV). Normalized EV/EBITDA at base IV is 9.72x, which is now within (not above) the corrected recent-normal-years range of 4.62x-9.94x, versus 11.46x pre-revision which was closer to the (higher) pre-revision ceiling of 11.9x. P/E 20.31x (on trough FY2026 EPS, understating true earnings power) sits below the recent-years average of 22.6x. P/S 2.06x is within the recent range. Base case upside (15.5% on IV; 12.7% probability-weighted) does not trigger any 'excessive upside at elevated price' trip -- the current price ($112.14) reflects a ~25% rally off the May-June 2026 selloff low (~$91.99) on the Apple/Qwen and DOJ-settlement news, but remains well below FY2018-2021 peak multiples and below sell-side price targets ($170-$192 as of July 2026). Net effect of the net-debt correction: intrinsic value rose in all three scenarios (base +2.8%, bull roughly flat/-0.03%, bear +66.9% in dollar terms / +21.4 points of upside) because the net-cash addition (RMB 260,828M) to the equity bridge outweighs the reduction in exit-multiple-implied terminal value from the lower, corrected caps (7.0/9.5/4.5x vs 9.0/11.5/6.0x) in every scenario. This is the honest combined result of two changes that point in opposite directions on EV but the same direction (up) on equity value, since the RMB 520,824M investment portfolio is real, liquid shareholder value that was previously omitted from the bridge entirely.
sanity_check.fix_applied: Exit multiple cap applied as a precautionary discipline even though no hard trip was triggered. REVISED 2026-07-26: caps recalibrated to 7.0x/9.5x/4.5x (base/bull/bear) from 9.0x/11.5x/6.0x, following the corrected (lower) historical EV/EBITDA range once the investment portfolio is properly netted out of EV. Base case 7.0x exit multiple on normalized EBITDA reduces base IV from an uncapped Gordon Growth figure to $129.55 (still an increase from the pre-revision capped figure of $125.97, because the net-cash correction more than offsets the lower cap). Bull case 9.5x cap similarly constrains the bull IV to $186.55 (essentially unchanged from $186.60 pre-revision -- the lower cap and the net-cash addition happen to roughly offset in the bull scenario, a coincidence of the specific numbers rather than a structural feature). The cap ensures no scenario implies EV/EBITDA meaningfully above what the market has paid in normal (non-bubble, non-trough) years, now measured on a fully-netted EV basis. Adjusted base used throughout (sensitivity, entry price, probability-weighted IV).
special_context: FY2026 is a deliberate investment trough -- anchoring on reported FCF (-46,609 RMB M) would produce systematic under-valuation. Mid-cycle normalization is methodologically correct, and July 2026 operating data (halved loss-per-order, guided ~50% FY2027 quick-commerce investment cut, AIDC near-breakeven, Cloud +40%) corroborates that the recovery is already underway.

WACC 11.5% incorporates ~2.5pp China/VIE/regulatory/litigation premium above a US-listed comparable. This remains the primary valuation lever -- if the DoD 1260H litigation resolves favorably (as Xiaomi/AMEC precedent suggests is plausible) and the Anthropic securities investigation does not mature into a filed suit, true WACC could fall toward 9.5-10.5% and base IV would rise further per the sensitivity matrix (though note the matrix is now WACC-driven only, since the exit cap binds across the full terminal-growth range tested).

The live FX update (6.7617 vs the prior model's 7.25) mechanically raises all USD-converted values by ~7.2% relative to an unchanged RMB valuation -- this is a real economic tailwind for USD-based ADS holders (RMB translation gain), not a modeling artifact, and is layered on top of (not instead of) the underlying operating assumptions.

EPS-based P/E multiples remain an imperfect anchor for BABA: FY2026 EPS ($6.38/ADS diluted) is still depressed by the investment cycle even though it improved from FY2025 levels in RMB terms due to one-off items; normalized run-rate earnings power is materially higher once quick-commerce losses fully abate and cloud operating leverage compounds.

Current stock price ($112.14) has rallied ~25% from the May-June 2026 trough (~$91.99) on the Apple/Qwen partnership and DOJ settlement, but remains meaningfully below sell-side price targets ($170-$192) and below the FY2018-2021 bubble-era multiples -- the market has re-rated on de-risking news but has not yet priced in full mid-cycle FCF recovery.

NET-DEBT CORRECTION (2026-07-26): This is a balance-sheet-bridge-only correction. Alibaba's balance sheet carries a very large treasury/investment portfolio (RMB 520,824M unrestricted short-term + other treasury investments, on top of RMB 131,530M cash) against RMB 259,996M of total debt -- a genuine net CASH position of RMB 260,828M, not the RMB 128,466M net DEBT figure used in the same-day pre-revision model. This portfolio is real, liquid (or near-liquid, with remaining maturities generally 1-5 years for the 'other treasury investments' bucket) shareholder value and belongs in both the equity bridge (added to EV to reach equity value) and the historical EV/EBITDA calibration series (netted out of EV, lowering historical and current multiples). Both were corrected in this revision for full internal consistency.
